reviews.body:
Good catch that Cohere was the one backend hard-coding `K: 0` and dropping `topp`. Storing both in `Configure` and only sending `P` when it's set is the right shape, and the `httptest` round-trip in `cohere_test.go` checks the actual request body, which is what matters here.

Two notes, neither blocking:

- Cohere's chat API documents `p` as 0.01 to 0.99 (I haven't verified this against a live call). `--topp 1.0` is a value people do set on other backends, so it may now get a 400 from Cohere where it used to be ignored. A clamp, or a line in the PR description, would cover it.
- Existing Cohere providers will start sampling with `k=50` (the `auth add` default) instead of `k=0`. That's the intent of the fix, so it's worth one sentence in the PR description for the changelog.

The `validate` check fails only on the title scope (this repo allows `deps` only), so `fix: pass configured topp/topk to the Cohere chat request` will clear it. Build and tests are green at `9bf8954`.

Thanks for the rename and the behaviour notes. Delta checked: `aa4ac43` has the same tree as `9bf8954`, only the commit message changed, and `validate`, build and tests are green now.

The one open point is the one you've already flagged in the description: `--topp 1.0` is now sent as `p=1.0`, and Cohere documents `p` as 0.01 to 0.99. Nobody has checked that against a live call yet, so I'll leave the final call on that to the maintainer rather than sign off. Clamping `P` to 0.99 in `GetCompletion` would close it if you want to make it a non-question.

Also, #1916 changes the `maxTokens` line in `CohereClient.Configure` right next to yours, so expect a small rebase for whichever lands second.

Thanks for merging `main` in, that settles the #1916 overlap. Delta checked: `0c37219` only brings in `main`, the Cohere change and its tests are identical to `aa4ac43`, and CI is green.

The one thing still open is the `p` range from last time: `--topp 1.0` goes out as `p=1.0`, and Cohere documents `p` as 0.01 to 0.99. Clamping `P` to 0.99 in `GetCompletion` (with a test case for it) makes it a non-question and I can sign off. Otherwise the approval stands and the maintainer makes the call.

Quick follow-up on the `p` range: I checked it against the SDK this repo pins. `cohere-go` v2.12.2 documents `p` on `ChatRequest` as min `0.01`, max `0.99` (and `k` as 0 to 500), so `--topp 1.0` would go out as an out-of-range `p=1.0`. Clamping `P` to 0.99 in `GetCompletion`, with a test for it, is still the one thing before I sign off.
